# `uuid_prefix_corpus.jsonl`

Real truncated-uuid token contexts, harvested by the truncated-uuid position
paper's scan, used to pin `shared.uuid_prefix.find_prefix_tokens` against
regression.

PRD `plans/uuid-prefix-resolution-prd.md` leaf alpha, contract C1. Generated by
`shared/tests/uuid_prefix_corpus_extract.py`; replayed by
`shared/tests/test_uuid_prefix_corpus.py`.

## What this corpus pins — and what it does not

Every expectation in it is the **detector's own answer**, machine-generated at
extraction time. Agreeing with them pins **regression-stability** and
**determinism**: the day a refactor quietly changes what the grammar accepts,
207 real contexts say so.

It does **not** pin correctness. Correctness is pinned by the hand-authored
grammar rows in `shared/tests/test_uuid_prefix.py`, decided by a human against
PRD section 4-C1. A machine-generated corpus that claimed correctness would be
a detector agreeing with itself. The markup corpus states the same split, and
it is repeated here because the distinction is the whole reason both files
exist.

The replay carries **one non-circular assertion** that never consults a stored
expectation: every row whose token is immediately preceded by `-` or `_` in the
window must yield no token at that span, re-derived from the window text. A
detector that dropped the glue rule could regenerate this whole file and pass
everything else; it cannot pass that.

## Never hand-write this file

Two rules, both load-bearing:

1. **The corpus is only ever produced by running the generator.** A hand-edited
   row asserts something no run ever produced, and every other assertion in the
   replay would agree with it.
2. **Every opening angle bracket in the emitted text is escaped as its
   `\u003c` JSON escape.**
   Standard JSON — `json.loads` decodes it transparently and the parsed value is
   byte-identical — but it means the file text carries no literal opening angle
   bracket, so a row quoted back into a tool call cannot carry an envelope
   literal. This README is written under the same rule.

## Record schema

One JSON object per line, eleven keys, all present on every record.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source_type` | str | Which store or tree the paper's scan read this text from. |
| `source_id` | str | The record id or file path within that source. |
| `field` | str | The field of that record the text came from. |
| `token` | str | The token the paper's scanner matched. |
| `window` | str | The real surrounding text, `text[start-40:end+40]`, token embedded. |
| `offset` | int | The token's offset **within `window`**. Never 0 — see below. |
| `kind` | str | `hex8` or `uuid36` — which of the paper's two occurrence tables. |
| `token_class` | str or null | The paper's class: `A`/`B`/`C`/`E`. Null for `uuid36`. |
| `glue` | str | `plain`, `hyphen` or `underscore` — the character before the token. |
| `expected_own_span` | bool | Machine-generated: is that exact span reported as a token? |
| `expected_tokens` | list | Machine-generated: the full document-ordered tuple for the window. |

The record is **self-contained**: the replay reads this file and nothing else —
no pickles, no live store, no network.

### Why `offset` is never 0

The paper's window is a plus/minus-40-character slice. A token sitting at index
0 had its true predecessor cut away by that truncation, so its glue verdict is
unknowable and any expectation there would be a guess wearing a measurement's
clothes. Those rows are dropped, as are rows whose token occurs twice in its own
window, where the paper's span is ambiguous.

## Strata

Coverage is asserted as *each declared stratum is non-empty*, never as a fixed
count, so a better corpus is never a regression. Twelve cells are populated at
207 rows: paper classes A/B/C/E crossed with the three glue contexts, plus full
uuids. Several are short because the population is: the paper found **four**
class-B occurrences in the entire scan, and only one class-C token glued to an
underscore. A quota that refused a short stratum would drop the rarest evidence
there is.

Selection is a fixed per-stratum quota off a stable sort key —
`(source_type, source_id, field, token, offset)` — with no RNG, so a re-run over
equal input is byte-identical and a regenerated corpus diffs to exactly the rows
that changed.

## Provenance, and why it cannot be re-derived

Cited, not re-measured (INV-9). The scan read live Mem0/Graphiti stores and
read-only task-db snapshots, and reported 47,209 8-hex occurrences and 23,631
full uuids, with each distinct 8-hex token classified A/B/C/E. **That scan is
not re-runnable**: the stores have moved on and the snapshots are gone. Its two
pickles — `occurrences.pkl` (31 MB) and `token_class.pkl` — are the only source.

They were found in the scan script's scratch directory under `/tmp`, which is
cleanable, so **this committed file is the durable artifact**. Nothing in the
test path reads the pickles.

To regenerate, put both pickles in `~/.cache/df-uuid-prefix-corpus/` (the
generator's default) or pass explicit paths:

    uv run --project shared python shared/tests/uuid_prefix_corpus_extract.py \
        --occurrences /path/to/occurrences.pkl \
        --token-class /path/to/token_class.pkl

The pickles must **never** be copied into the repo: 31 MB of pickled corpus is
not a fixture, and a stray `.pkl` under `shared/` would be swept into a commit.
